sources.title: Good Housekeeping grilled chicken and herbed corn

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired grilled chicken showcases summer corn charred directly on the grill until the kernels develop smoky, caramelized spots. The herb salsa combines fresh basil and mint with lemon and Parmesan, creating a bright, aromatic topping. The lemon's acidity cuts through the rich fat of chicken thighs.

## Directions

1.  **The Chicken:** Preheat grill to medium-high. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Grill, skin-side down first, for 15-20 minutes total, turning once, until the skin is crispy and internal temp reaches 165°F.
2.  **The Corn:** Place corn ears directly on the grill. Cook for 10 minutes, rotating occasionally, until charred in spots.
3.  **The Salsa:** While grilling, place basil, mint, Parmesan, and garlic in a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped. Drizzle in the lemon juice and olive oil and pulse once more until a chunky emulsion forms.
4.  **Combine:** Shear the charred kernels off the cobs. In a small bowl, toss the kernels with the herb sauce.
5.  **Serve:** Place grilled chicken on a platter and top generously with the herbed corn salsa. Serve immediately.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired grilled chicken showcases summer corn charred directly on the grill until the kernels develop smoky, caramelized spots. The herb salsa combines fresh basil and mint with lemon and Parmesan, creating a bright, aromatic topping. The lemon's acidity cuts through the rich fat of chicken thighs.

## Directions

1. **Grill chicken:** Preheat the grill to medium-high. Season all the thighs with the listed salt and pepper allowance. Grill skin-side down first, turning as the surface browns; start checking at 15–20 minutes total and continue until the thickest part of each thigh reaches 165°F / 74°C, away from the bone. Move away from flare-ups or excessive direct heat. Transfer cooked chicken with clean utensils to a clean platter.
2. **Grill corn:** Grill all the shucked corn, rotating occasionally, for about 10 minutes, until the kernels are tender and charred in spots. Keep ready-to-eat corn away from raw chicken and its utensils.
3. **Make herb sauce:** While grilling, pulse all the basil, mint, Parmesan and garlic in a clean food processor until finely chopped. Add all the lemon juice and olive oil and pulse just to combine. Season with the listed salt allowance to taste.
4. **Combine:** When the corn is safe to handle, cut all its kernels off the cobs into a bowl and mix them with all the herb sauce.
5. **Serve:** Divide the chicken and complete corn-herb topping among the listed portions and serve promptly.
